newsitem.title: USA: Orlando, Fla., to sell $40 mln indexed muni bonds.
newsitem.headline: Orlando, Fla., to sell $40 mln indexed muni bonds.

text.p: Orlando, Fla., said Thursday it plans to sell $40 million of inflation-indexed, tax-exempt bonds through a negotiated sale led by Goldman Sachs & Co.
Orlando said in a statement that the offering was the first of its kind for the municipal market.
Orlando said the bonds, called Muni CPIs, were based on the U.S. Treasury Inflation-Indexed-Proctection Series bonds (TIPS), which were first offered in late January.
As with TIPs, the investor's income will track changes in the consumer price index.
The income on the Orlando bonds would be exempt from federal taxation. The bonds will pay a semi-annnual coupon that will fluctuate with changes in the CPI.

The interest payments City of Orlando owes to investors will increase if inflation rates rise, but the city said it plans to hedge this risk by entering into an interest rate sweap agreement with Goldman Sachs.
